newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING - SYKORA WINS SEASON'S FIRST WORLD CUP MEN'S SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING - SYKORA WINS SEASON'S FIRST WORLD CUP MEN'S SLALOM.

text.p: Thomas Sykora won the season's first World Cup slalom for men Sunday, picking up where he left off last spring and leading a one-two sweep by the powerful Austrian team.

Sykora won with a time of 1:46.03, just ahead of teammate Thomas Stangassinger, who clocked 1:46.32. Kjetil Andre Aaamodt of Norway finished third in 1:46.91 and took over the overall World Cup lead after two races.
Austria also claimed fourth place with Christian Mayer and sixth with Michael Tritscher. Another Norwegian, Ole Christian Furuseth, was fifth.
Sykora won last season's concluding slalom at the World Cup finals in Lillehammer, Norway, and his confidence is soaring.

"I was able to relax all summer, to have my very best training," said Sykora, who finished third in last season's slalom standings despite a slow start and an illness later that caused him to falter at the world championships. Sykora has won three of the last five World Cup slalom races.
""My goal now is to win the World Cup slalom title," said the 28-year-old veteran of six seasons. "I am skiing so consistently that I can take all the risks and make it."
On Sunday, he had the added advantage of having another Austrian, Stangassinger, already at the finish in first place, with Mayer then third.
"Since I knew Austria already had the victory, I could go for it without fear."
Stangassinger seemed almost as happy with second place, his best finish in a year. He has not won a race since his Olympic championship at Lillehammer in 1994.
His victory drought was largely the result of an injured shoulder and difficulties with his skis. Now, with new equipment and a fresh attitude, he believes he can return to the top.
"It is like a new wind blowing behind me. This is a great start."

The Austrians, who have a stunningly strong stable of slalom racers, expected to do well. Not so Aamodt, who struggled through two substandard seasons after winning the overall title, and three Olympic medals, in 1994.
"I was surprised, since I had no idea about my form in slalom," said Aamodt, who slipped to fifth in the overall standings in 1995 and a lagging 10th last season.
Aamodt now has the early lead with 120 points. Steve Locher of Switzerland and Sykora each have 100 points.

The Park City programme will conclude Monday with a men's giant slalom, postponed from Friday. The World Cup men's focus then will switch to Breckenridge, Colorado, for a Saturday giant slalom and Sunday slalom.
